identity.name: JM FINANCIAL LIMITED
identity.industry: Diversified Financial Services — Investment Banking / Capital Markets, Private Credit (incl. ARC/distressed), Wealth & Asset Management, Affordable Home Loans

summary.oneLiner: Two years into its strategic pivot (announced May 2024), JM Financial has delivered broad-based revenue/profit growth across all four "grow" segments (CACM +26% 2-yr revenue, Wealth +17%, Asset Mgmt +38%, Affordable Home Loans +37%) while deliberately de-risking/shrinking the legacy Private Markets balance sheet (loan book down from ₹10,000 cr in FY24 to ₹4,000 cr in FY26). Q4/Q1 FY27 near-term optics are muddied by an FPI-selling-driven capital-markets slowdown (near-zero deal activity in March-April, reviving mid-April), but management expects a much stronger H2 FY27 as the IPO/QIP/block pipeline (~₹1,40,000 cr filed, seen doubling to ~₹2,00,000 cr by October) converts once volatility eases.

one-line thesis: Two years into its strategic pivot (announced May 2024), JM Financial has delivered broad-based revenue/profit growth across all four "grow" segments (CACM +26% 2-yr revenue, Wealth +17%, Asset Mgmt +38%, Affordable Home Loans +37%) while deliberately de-risking/shrinking the legacy Private Markets balance sheet (loan book down from ₹10,000 cr in FY24 to ₹4,000 cr in FY26). Q4/Q1 FY27 near-term optics are muddied by an FPI-selling-driven capital-markets slowdown (near-zero deal activity in March-April, reviving mid-April), but management expects a much stronger H2 FY27 as the IPO/QIP/block pipeline (~₹1,40,000 cr filed, seen doubling to ~₹2,00,000 cr by October) converts once volatility eases.

| Metric | FY26 (full year) | YoY | Note |

| Gross margin | Not disclosed at consol level | — | Segment PBT/ROE given instead (see §5) |
| Order book | CACM: 41 capital-markets transactions closed (~₹95,000 cr) in FY26; 55 IPO filings (~₹1,40,000 cr issue size); pipeline seen doubling to ~₹2,00,000 cr by Oct-2026 | — | Pipeline strength ≠ near-term execution — mgmt flags 7-8 months of market visibility needed to convert |

> Consol. net worth (ex-minority) ₹10,605 cr → book value ~₹111/share. FY26 dividend ~₹5.95/share (₹570 cr aggregate over trailing 4 quarters), against a stated policy of distributing 50% of Private Markets PAT as dividend.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- Private Markets recovery: reiterated ₹250-300 cr/year target for FY26/27/28 — FY26 delivered >₹270 cr, "pretty much on target" for FY27.
- Private Markets standard loan book: grow 15-20% YoY — target ~₹5,000 cr by March 2027 (from ~₹4,000 cr); distressed credit (₹3,665 cr) to grow ~15%; equity+alternatives capped at ≤20% of total ~₹13,000 cr book.
- Target segment return assumptions given: standard loans 13-14%, distressed credit 16-18%, equity/alternatives 15-16%.
- Wealth Management: net inflows targeted at ~20% AUM growth (~₹6,000 cr) for FY27, excluding mark-to-market; standalone (ex-broking) business targeted to break even in FY27, with digital (BlinkX) cost base to be "cut down significantly" over the next 3-6 months.
- Group-level long-term target: 15% revenue growth and 15% ROE (mgmt: "we are kind of there" on an investment-cycle-adjusted basis).
- Affordable Home Loans: IPO targeted by 2028-29; AUM to keep growing ~25% YoY.
- CACM: no explicit revenue guidance — management asks investors to model this segment "peak-to-peak" (targets doubling the business every 4-5 years) given quarter-to-quarter volatility from deal-timing.
- No demerger/listing of individual segments planned in the near term ("maybe after a year or 2 years").
order book & pipeline: CACM pipeline ~₹1,40,000 cr of filed IPOs (55 filings) plus a growing non-IPO pipeline (QIPs, blocks, M&A, PE placements); management expects this to nearly double YoY (June-Sept 2025 base vs June-Oct 2026) to ~₹2,00,000 cr. FPI selling (~4-5 months) has stalled conversion — deal activity was near-zero in March-April 2026, with a mid-April revival; management expects H2 FY27 to be materially stronger as a ~6-month lag typically drives corporates from equity issuance toward credit/PE placements when equity markets stay shut. Asset Management: first performing-credit AIF (~₹347 cr committed) is one deal from full deployment; second performing-credit fund ("Select Credit") and a pre-IPO fund are in roadshow, pre-IPO fund near first close (total raise target >₹1,000 cr), to be followed by a PE fund targeting a similar raise.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **CACM** (IB + institutional equities): FY26 net revenue ₹789 cr (+11% YoY), opex-adjusted PAT ₹347 cr, capital employed ₹829 cr → ROE ~47%. Q4FY26 segment PAT only ₹39 cr — hit by the primary-issuance drought. Research coverage expanded to ~400 stocks active + ~150 soft coverage, cited as the largest on the Street; new derivatives desk added to institutional equities last year.
- **Private Markets**: FY26 operating PBT +3.5x to ₹742 cr, PAT (post-minority) +3.6x to ₹543 cr on capital employed ~₹6,600 cr; Q4FY26 segment PAT (post-minority) ₹78 cr. Loan book down from ₹10,000 cr (FY24) → ₹5,000 cr (FY25) → ₹4,000 cr (FY26), driven by real-estate repayments/prepayments; management now pivoting to a fee-based, syndication-led model rather than growing an on-balance-sheet lending book (self-capped debt:equity of 2:1–3:1).
- **Wealth Management**: FY26 net revenue ₹775 cr (+9% YoY), PAT ₹132 cr, capital employed ₹1,157 cr → ROE ~12%; Q4FY26 segment PAT ₹39 cr (hit by market volatility). RM/sales headcount +30% YoY to 1,046; branches +10 to 72; franchisees to 874. Recurring AUM ~₹31,000 cr (+10% YoY, 29% of total); overall Wealth AUM >₹1,00,000 cr. Revenue split ~50% recurring (fees/commission/interest) vs ~50% transactional (broking + other); broking-only ROE 25-30% given smaller capital base; margin trade finance book grew from ₹300-400 cr to ~₹2,000 cr.
- **Asset Management**: FY26 revenue +38% YoY; MF management fees +65% to ~₹44 cr; segment loss (post-minority) ~₹30 cr for FY26, Q4FY26 loss ₹5 cr — still in an investment/scaling phase (management flags AM has the highest operating leverage once profitable, ~2-year runway to breakeven). Non-liquid MF average AUM ~₹10,500 cr; AM headcount +17% YoY to 217.
- **Affordable Home Loans**: FY26 revenue +25% YoY to ₹455 cr; PAT (post-minority) +45% to ₹74 cr; capital employed ~₹833 cr; Q4FY26 segment PAT ₹25 cr. AUM +22% YoY to ~₹3,460-3,500 cr; branch network 151; customer base >33,000; gross NPA 0.5%, collection efficiency 99.4%.
growth verticals / optionality: Cross-segment "flywheel": IB transaction clients feed Wealth Management account openings (transactional revenue), which convert to recurring AUM over time; Wealth referrals into the investment bank are also rising ("reverse origination"). Asset Management AIF platform (performing credit, Select Credit, pre-IPO, upcoming PE fund) is a multi-year optionality layer once each fund scales past its investment phase.
6a. moat & competitive position (optiona:
- Research breadth: ~400 stocks active coverage + ~150 soft coverage — management claims no Tier-1 bank on the Street matches this, used as a client-acquisition/differentiation lever for CACM.
- Rank claim: management states JM is "number 1, number 2 and number 3 across products" as a deal house (unquantified — no independent league-table citation given on the call).
- 54-year operating history cited as basis for resilience through market-volatility cycles (qualitative, not evidenced with data).
margins & cost dynamics: CACM employee cost rose ₹165 cr → ₹265 cr (FY24→FY26, +₹100 cr) against a ₹259 cr revenue increase over the same period and a ~₹100 cr PAT increase — management frames this as deliberate front-loading of hiring (incl. new derivatives desk, expanded research) ahead of a pipeline that grew from ~₹40,000-50,000 cr to ~₹1,40,000 cr. Digital investment (BlinkX) of ₹40-50 cr/year is being "cut down significantly" over the next 3-6 months, expected to show savings from Q1FY27 itself. Wealth Management margin expansion is the explicit FY27 focus as newly-hired RM productivity ramps.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): No physical capex discussed; the "expansion" here is people/franchisee-led — Wealth branches +10 to 72, franchisees to 874, RM headcount +30% YoY (most hires spread through the year, so productivity gains expected to phase in over the next 3-6 months — watch for slippage on this timeline next quarter).
capital allocation: Dividend policy: 50% of Private Markets PAT distributed annually; ₹570 cr aggregate dividend paid/proposed over trailing 4 quarters (~₹5.95/share). Freed-up capital from Private Markets book de-risking is being redirected first to Wealth & Asset Management, then Affordable Home Loans; CACM and Private Markets are self-funding and require no fresh capital. No demerger/listing of individual businesses in the near term, despite investor prompting (peer comparisons of listed broking + wealth-management spin-offs) — management wants scale first.
risks & watch-items:
- FPI ownership in Indian equities down to ~15% from a high of ~19% — a swing factor for CACM/Private-Markets deal conversion timing.
- Geopolitical/oil-price overhang (West Asia crisis, oil ~$90-100) cited as a driver of the FPI-selling episode and IPO-market pause through Q4FY26/Q1FY27.
- Real-estate lending: management explicitly staying cautious/slow ("risk-adjusted returns... not attractive enough"), flags the up-cycle in real estate sales as over — a read-through risk for real-estate-linked private credit peers too.
- Wealth Management ROE still subdued (~12%) after 3 years of talent/infrastructure investment — productivity ramp is unproven until it shows in FY27 numbers.
- Asset Management still loss-making (~₹30 cr FY26), multi-year runway to profitability.
management quality / tone: Confident/promotional tone throughout, with explicit multi-year framing ("model CACM/Private Markets peak-to-peak") to pre-empt quarter-to-quarter volatility concerns. Management proactively disclosed one-off items (tax-refund interest, Labour Code impact) and gave granular segment/AUM/loan-book breakdowns (e.g., full Private Markets book composition on request) rather than deflecting. Fielded a pointed analyst question on CACM employee-cost-vs-revenue math directly rather than avoiding it.
non-obvious takeaways:
- Bajaj Allianz's June-2025 purchase of 2.1% of JM Financial Home Loans at ₹48/share implies a ₹3,100 cr valuation for the Affordable Home Loans subsidiary alone — an external, market-set data point for sum-of-the-parts investors.
- Management explicitly separates "loan book" optics from revenue: interest income has de-grown for two years purely due to deliberate real-estate book runoff, which depresses consolidated revenue even as every operating segment grows — a case where headline consol. revenue is a poor proxy for underlying momentum.
- Real estate lending will stop being reported as a standalone bucket going forward — it will be folded into the overall standard/corporate loan book (management will still disclose the real-estate % of total), signaling declining strategic emphasis on that vertical as a distinct business line.

hero.oneLiner: Two years into its strategic pivot (announced May 2024), JM Financial has delivered broad-based revenue/profit growth across all four "grow" segments (CACM +26% 2-yr revenue, Wealth +17%, Asset Mgmt +38%, Affordable Home Loans +37%) while deliberately de-risking/shrinking the legacy Private Markets balance sheet (loan book down from ₹10,000 cr in FY24 to ₹4,000 cr in FY26). Q4/Q1 FY27 near-term optics are muddied by an FPI-selling-driven capital-markets slowdown (near-zero deal activity in March-April, reviving mid-April), but management expects a much stronger H2 FY27 as the IPO/QIP/block pipeline (~₹1,40,000 cr filed, seen doubling to ~₹2,00,000 cr by October) converts once volatility eases.
